item.content:encoded:
The Eric Bleumink Scholarship 2027 offers an exciting opportunity for talented international students to pursue an eligible Master’s degree at the University of Groningen in the Netherlands.

The scholarship is intended for academically outstanding students and provides financial support toward major costs associated with studying abroad. It is an excellent opportunity for students seeking a fully funded Master’s opportunity in Europe and looking to study at an internationally recognised research university.

About the Eric Bleumink Scholarship

The Eric Bleumink Scholarship provides talented students from around the world with the opportunity to undertake postgraduate studies at the University of Groningen.

The scholarship is particularly valuable for international students who have strong academic records and require financial support to pursue their studies.

Selected students can benefit from financial assistance covering several important costs, allowing them to concentrate on their academic development and make the most of their experience in the Netherlands.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The Eric Bleumink Scholarship offers extensive financial support. According to the provided opportunity information, the benefits include:

  • Full tuition fee coverage
  • International travel expenses
  • Living expenses
  • Health insurance
  • Books and study materials
  • Financial support for academic expenses
  • The opportunity to study at a leading European research university
  • Access to an international academic environment and network

These benefits can substantially reduce the financial challenges associated with pursuing a Master’s degree abroad.

Available Master’s Programmes

The scholarship is available for eligible Master’s programmes offered by the University of Groningen.

Potential areas of study include:

Arts and Humanities

Students interested in humanities, culture, languages, history, and related disciplines may find eligible programmes within this broad field.

Business and Economics

The university offers opportunities for students interested in business, economics, management, and related areas.

Law

Students interested in legal studies can explore eligible Master’s programmes in law and related disciplines.

Science and Engineering

The opportunity also covers eligible programmes within science, technology, engineering, and related fields.

Social Sciences

Students interested in society, politics, development, international relations, and related disciplines can explore relevant programmes.

Medical and Health Sciences

Eligible programmes may also be available in medical and health-related fields.

Environmental Sciences

Students interested in environmental issues, sustainability, climate, and related areas can explore eligible programmes.

Information Technology

Applicants interested in technology, computing, and information systems may also find eligible Master’s programmes.

Education

Eligible graduate programmes in education and related areas are also included.

Important: Applicants should verify that their chosen Master’s programme is eligible and meets the specific admission requirements of the University of Groningen.

Who Is Eligible?

The scholarship is intended for international students applying for eligible Master’s programmes at the University of Groningen.

Applicants should generally:

  • Be an international student.
  • Apply for an eligible Master’s programme at the University of Groningen.
  • Have an outstanding academic record.
  • Demonstrate financial need.
  • Meet the university’s English-language requirements.
  • Provide strong academic or professional recommendations where required.
  • Meet the admission requirements of their selected Master’s programme.
  • Be committed to successfully completing the programme.

Because Master’s programmes can have different requirements, applicants should carefully check the conditions attached to their specific programme.

Academic Excellence

Academic performance is an important consideration for this opportunity. Prospective applicants should ensure that their academic records clearly demonstrate their ability to succeed in postgraduate study.

A strong academic profile, together with a well-prepared admission application, can help applicants present themselves competitively.

English Language Requirements

Applicants must meet the English-language requirements associated with their chosen Master’s programme.

Depending on the programme, applicants may be required to provide evidence of English proficiency through an accepted language test or another recognised form of evidence.

Students should check the requirements of their specific programme before submitting their application.

Documents to Prepare

Applicants should prepare the documents required for admission to their selected Master’s programme. These may include:

  • Academic transcripts
  • Degree certificates
  • Curriculum vitae (CV)
  • Motivation letter or personal statement
  • Recommendation letters
  • Valid passport or national identification document
  • English-language proficiency certificate
  • Proof of financial circumstances, where required
  • Other programme-specific documents

Applicants should ensure that all documents are accurate, complete, and prepared according to the university’s instructions.

How the Scholarship Application Works

One important feature of the Eric Bleumink Scholarship is that there is no separate scholarship application according to the information provided.

Instead, eligible candidates are considered for nomination through the Master’s admission process.

Step 1: Choose a Master’s Programme

First, identify an eligible Master’s programme at the University of Groningen that matches your academic background and career goals.

Step 2: Check the Admission Requirements

Carefully review the programme’s academic, language, and documentation requirements.

Step 3: Prepare Your Documents

Gather your transcripts, degree certificates, CV, motivation statement, recommendations, and other required documents.

Step 4: Submit Your Master’s Application

Complete and submit your application for admission to the University of Groningen before the relevant deadline.

Step 5: Scholarship Consideration

Eligible and outstanding candidates may be nominated by the university for the Eric Bleumink Scholarship.

This means applicants should focus on submitting a strong and complete Master’s admission application.

Why Study in the Netherlands?

Studying in the Netherlands can provide international students with an opportunity to experience a highly international academic environment while gaining advanced knowledge and skills.

The country is home to internationally recognised universities and offers a diverse learning environment that brings together students and researchers from different parts of the world.

For students interested in building an international academic and professional network, studying in the Netherlands can be a valuable experience.

Why Choose the University of Groningen?

The University of Groningen is one of the Netherlands’ longstanding research universities and offers a broad selection of Master’s programmes.

Students have the opportunity to study in an international academic environment while engaging with research, innovation, and interdisciplinary learning.

The university’s international community can also provide students with opportunities to build connections with peers and academics from different countries and academic backgrounds.

Application Timeline

Prospective applicants should pay close attention to the application timeline.

Master’s application deadline for consideration:
📅 December 1, 2026

Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing their applications early. Waiting until the final days can create unnecessary pressure, particularly if academic documents, recommendation letters, language test results, or other supporting materials are required.

Important Note for Applicants

The scholarship information provided states that eligible candidates are considered for the fellowship after applying for admission and that there is no separate scholarship application.

Therefore, applicants should not assume that submitting a general scholarship form is necessary. Instead, they should carefully follow the University of Groningen’s Master’s admission process and confirm the latest requirements for their selected programme.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Eric Bleumink Scholarship fully funded?

The provided scholarship information describes the opportunity as fully funded and lists support for tuition, international travel, living expenses, health insurance, books, and study materials.

Who can apply?

The opportunity is aimed at international students seeking admission to eligible Master’s programmes at the University of Groningen.

Is there a separate scholarship application?

No. According to the provided information, eligible candidates are considered for nomination after applying for admission to an eligible Master’s programme.

What level of study is supported?

The scholarship supports eligible Master’s degree programmes.

Which subjects are available?

Eligible programmes span areas such as Arts and Humanities, Business and Economics, Law, Science, Engineering, Social Sciences, Medical Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Information Technology, Education, and other eligible graduate programmes.

When is the deadline?

The application deadline stated in the provided information is December 1, 2026.

Where is the scholarship located?

The scholarship is hosted by the University of Groningen in the Netherlands.

Conclusion

The Eric Bleumink Scholarship 2027 is a valuable opportunity for academically strong international students who want to pursue a Master’s degree in the Netherlands without carrying the full financial burden of international study.

Beyond financial support, the opportunity can provide students with access to an international academic environment, research opportunities, and a diverse network of students and scholars.

If you are considering postgraduate study in Europe, this is an opportunity worth exploring. Start by identifying an eligible Master’s programme, reviewing its admission requirements, preparing your supporting documents, and submitting your application well before the December 1, 2026 deadline.

Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship in Sustainability 2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for early-career scholars who are passionate about sustainability, rigorous academic research, and creating meaningful real-world impact.

Hosted by Cornell University, the fellowship brings together academic research and practical sustainability action by giving Fellows the opportunity to work with both a Cornell faculty mentor and a partnering external organization.

The program is designed for researchers who want to move beyond academic research alone and explore how rigorous scholarship can contribute to solutions for some of the world’s most pressing sustainability challenges.

Successful Fellows will become part of the Cornell Atkinson community and participate in the Sustainability Leadership Program, where they join a cohort of early-career scholars and receive specialized support in areas such as science communication, strategic career planning, and collaborative leadership.

Applications are now being invited for the 2027 Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship in Sustainability.

About the Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship

The Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship is structured around the idea that sustainability research should connect strong academic scholarship with measurable impact in the real world.

Rather than focusing exclusively on traditional academic research, the fellowship encourages scholars to work across academic and external settings.

Each Fellow works with:

  • A Cornell faculty mentor
  • An external advisor
  • A partnering external organization

This structure provides Fellows with an opportunity to connect their research with organizations and communities beyond the university.

The program welcomes research proposals from early-career scholars working within any of Cornell Atkinson’s four primary research areas.

Applicants are encouraged to develop projects that demonstrate both academic rigor and the potential to contribute to meaningful sustainability outcomes.

Fellowship Duration

The Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship is a:

Three-year, 12-month appointment at Cornell University.

This means Fellows participate in a full-time postdoctoral appointment for three years, with each year structured as a 12-month appointment.

The three-year structure provides Fellows with sufficient time to:

  • Develop their research
  • Conduct rigorous investigations
  • Work with their Cornell mentor
  • Collaborate with external partners
  • Produce research outputs
  • Build professional networks
  • Develop leadership skills
  • Translate research into real-world impact

Fellowship Salary and Financial Support

Successful Fellows receive a competitive financial package.

Annual Salary

Fellows receive:

$65,000 per year

This salary is provided throughout the fellowship appointment.

Cornell Employee Benefits

Fellows will also receive:

Full Cornell employee benefits

These benefits are provided as part of the postdoctoral appointment and are in addition to the annual salary.

Research and Travel Funding

Each Fellow receives:

$12,000 per year

for research- and travel-related expenses.

This additional funding can support activities connected with the Fellow’s research and professional development, including eligible research expenses and travel associated with academic or professional activities.

Over three years, the research and travel allocation totals up to:

$36,000

in addition to the annual salary and employee benefits.

Residency and Location Requirements

An important requirement of the Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship is that Fellows must maintain their primary residence in Ithaca, New York, for the duration of their appointment.

Fellows must also spend the majority of their time on the Cornell University campus.

This requirement exists so that Fellows can fully participate in Cornell Atkinson activities, interact with their colleagues and mentors, and engage with the broader Cornell research community.

Remote and Hybrid Appointments

The program does not permit:

  • Fully remote appointments
  • Hybrid postdoctoral appointments

Applicants should therefore be prepared to relocate to or maintain their primary residence in Ithaca, New York, and participate substantially in on-campus activities.

This is an important consideration for applicants currently living outside Ithaca or outside the United States.

Sustainability Leadership Program

A major component of the Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship is participation in the Sustainability Leadership Program.

Through this program, Fellows become part of a cohort of early-career scholars working on sustainability-related research and challenges.

The program provides curated professional development in areas including:

Science Communication

Fellows receive support in communicating complex research to audiences beyond specialized academic communities.

Effective science communication can help researchers:

  • Explain research clearly
  • Reach policymakers and practitioners
  • Engage communities
  • Communicate with non-specialist audiences
  • Increase the practical impact of research findings

Strategic Career Planning

Fellows receive guidance to help them think strategically about their professional development and future career paths.

Collaborative Leadership

The program also develops collaborative leadership skills, helping Fellows work effectively with researchers, institutions, organizations, and other stakeholders.

Research Focus and Sustainability

The Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship invites research proposals from early-career scholars working within Cornell Atkinson’s four primary research areas.

Applicants should ensure that their proposed project aligns with at least one of the Center’s priority areas.

The program is particularly suited to scholars whose research can connect rigorous academic investigation with practical sustainability outcomes.

A strong proposal should demonstrate:

  • A clearly defined research challenge
  • Rigorous research methods
  • A meaningful sustainability connection
  • Potential real-world impact
  • A strong academic foundation
  • A clear relationship with the proposed Cornell advisor
  • Meaningful engagement with an external partner

Academic and External Collaboration

One of the distinctive features of this fellowship is its dual-mentorship and partnership model.

Each proposed project requires both academic and external collaboration.

Applicants are asked to identify:

  1. A proposed Cornell faculty advisor
  2. A proposed external advisor
  3. An external partner organization

This structure enables Fellows to connect university-based research with organizations working outside the traditional academic environment.

The external partner may provide an important pathway for translating research findings into practice, policy, innovation, organizational change, or other forms of real-world sustainability impact.

Who Should Apply?

The fellowship is intended for early-career scholars interested in sustainability research and real-world impact.

Applicants should be pursuing or have completed a PhD and must provide a known or anticipated month and year of PhD graduation in the application.

The program is particularly appropriate for researchers who:

  • Are at the early stage of their research careers
  • Have a strong research background
  • Are developing an independent research agenda
  • Want to work at the intersection of research and sustainability
  • Are interested in translating research into real-world impact
  • Can identify an appropriate Cornell faculty mentor
  • Can establish a meaningful relationship with an external organization
  • Are willing to work primarily on campus in Ithaca

Application Requirements

Applicants must complete the online application and submit the required materials by the deadline.

The application requires several important components.

1. Applicant Information

Applicants must provide:

  • Full name
  • Email address
  • Current university or organization
  • Project title

2. Project Abstract

Applicants must provide a clear summary of their proposed project.

The abstract should explain:

  • The proposed research
  • The methods that will be used
  • The anticipated impact

The abstract has a strict limit of:

250 words maximum

Applicants should therefore make the abstract focused, clear, and informative.

3. Alignment With Cornell Atkinson Priority Areas

Applicants must indicate which of Cornell Atkinson’s priority research areas their project addresses.

The application allows applicants to select all applicable areas.

Applicants should carefully demonstrate how their proposed research aligns with the Center’s sustainability priorities.

4. Proposed Cornell Advisor

Applicants must identify a proposed Cornell faculty advisor.

The application requires:

  • Cornell advisor’s name
  • Cornell advisor’s email address

The proposed advisor should be appropriately positioned to provide academic mentorship relevant to the proposed research.

5. Proposed External Advisor

Applicants must also identify an external advisor.

The application requires:

  • External advisor’s name
  • External advisor’s email address

This reinforces the fellowship’s emphasis on connecting academic research with external expertise and real-world application.

6. External Partner Organization

Applicants must identify an:

External Partner Organization

The external partnership is an important component of the fellowship because Fellows are expected to work at the intersection of academic research and practical sustainability impact.

Applicants may also list additional external partners where applicable.

7. PhD Graduation Date

Applicants must provide their:

Month and year of PhD graduation

The application accepts either a known graduation date or an anticipated graduation date.

Applicants should provide accurate information based on their academic status.

8. Proposal Packet

Applicants must upload one PDF document containing the complete proposal packet.

The proposal packet must include:

  • Applicant Background
  • Description of Proposed Project
  • Impact Statement
  • Curriculum Vitae

Applicants should not upload these documents as separate attachments.

The application specifically requires them to be combined into a single PDF proposal packet.

Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must arrange for four recommendation letters to be submitted directly to Cornell Atkinson.

The four required recommenders are:

  1. Proposed Cornell Advisor
  2. Proposed External Advisor
  3. PhD Advisor
  4. One Other Recommender

All four letters must be submitted directly to:

atkinson-postdoc@cornell.edu

by the application deadline.

Applicants should contact their recommenders well in advance to ensure that the letters are submitted on time.

Recommendation Letter Deadline

All four recommendation letters must arrive by:

5 p.m. ET on October 20, 2026

Letters received after the application deadline will not be accepted.

Applicants should therefore not wait until the final day to contact their recommenders.

Application Deadline

The complete application must be submitted by:

October 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time

This is the official application deadline for the 2027 Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship.

Applicants should ensure that:

  • The online application is completed
  • The proposal packet is uploaded
  • Required information is provided
  • Four recommendation letters have been requested
  • Recommendation letters are submitted directly to Cornell
  • The application is submitted before the deadline

Important Application Rules

Applicants should pay close attention to the program’s submission requirements.

Applications Cannot Be Edited After Submission

The application form can be saved as a draft while applicants are working on it.

However, once the application has been submitted:

It cannot be edited.

Applicants should carefully review all information and attachments before submitting.

Late Applications

Late applications will not be reviewed.

The deadline is:

October 20, 2026 at 5 p.m. ET

Applicants should plan to submit before the final hours of the application period to avoid technical or administrative problems.

Incomplete Applications

Incomplete applications will not be reviewed.

Applicants should use the application requirements as a checklist to ensure that every required component has been addressed.

Suggested Application Preparation Checklist

Before submitting, applicants should confirm that they have completed the following:

  • Applicant name
  • Applicant email
  • Current university or organization
  • Project title
  • 250-word project abstract
  • Cornell Atkinson priority-area selection
  • Proposed Cornell advisor
  • Cornell advisor email
  • Proposed external advisor
  • External advisor email
  • External partner organization
  • Additional external partners, if applicable
  • Month and year of PhD graduation
  • Single PDF proposal packet
  • Applicant background
  • Proposed project description
  • Impact statement
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Cornell advisor recommendation
  • External advisor recommendation
  • PhD advisor recommendation
  • Fourth recommendation
  • Final application review
  • Application submitted before 5 p.m. ET on October 20, 2026

What Makes This Fellowship Different?

The Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship stands out because it combines several dimensions of professional development and research.

Rather than providing only a traditional postdoctoral research appointment, the program connects Fellows with:

  • Cornell academic mentorship
  • External organizational collaboration
  • Sustainability research
  • Leadership development
  • Science communication training
  • Strategic career planning
  • Collaborative leadership development
  • Research and travel funding

This creates an environment in which early-career researchers can develop both as scholars and as leaders capable of translating research into meaningful action.

Real-World Impact and Sustainability

The fellowship is particularly suited to researchers who want their work to contribute to solutions beyond academic publications.

The combination of a Cornell faculty mentor and an external partner gives Fellows an opportunity to consider how research can influence:

  • Policy
  • Practice
  • Innovation
  • Organizations
  • Communities
  • Sustainability decision-making

Applicants should therefore think carefully about the practical significance of their research and clearly explain the potential impact in their proposal.

Professional Development Opportunities

In addition to conducting research, Fellows benefit from professional development through the Sustainability Leadership Program.

The program’s focus on science communication can help researchers become more effective communicators.

Strategic career planning can help Fellows make informed decisions about their future professional direction.

Collaborative leadership training can help researchers build the skills necessary to work across disciplines and sectors.

Together, these elements can help prepare Fellows for careers in:

  • Academia
  • Research
  • Government
  • Nonprofit organizations
  • Industry
  • Sustainability organizations
  • Policy
  • Science communication
  • Other research and impact-oriented careers

Fellowship Location

The fellowship is based at:

Cornell University, Ithaca, New York, USA

Fellows must maintain primary residency in Ithaca throughout the appointment and spend the majority of their time on campus.

Applicants who require a remote or hybrid arrangement should note that these arrangements are not permitted for Cornell Atkinson postdoctoral Fellows.Position Information

The fellowship is listed as:

Position: Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship in Sustainability

Requisition Number: 32295

Hiring Department: Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability

Application Deadline: October 20, 2026 at 5 p.m. ET

                                      Read Full Details HERE

How to Apply

Applicants should complete the official Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship application form and upload their complete proposal packet as one PDF.

Applicants must also ensure that all four required recommenders submit their letters directly to Cornell Atkinson before the deadline.

For questions about the fellowship or application form, applicants can contact:

atkinson-postdoc@cornell.edu

Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing their proposal and contacting recommenders well before the deadline.

Important Deadline

October 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET

Both the application and all required recommendation letters must be submitted by the deadline.

Late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed.

                                                    A𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐲 HERE

Conclusion

The Cornell Atkinson Postdoctoral Fellowship in Sustainability 2027 presents a significant opportunity for early-career scholars seeking to combine rigorous academic research with practical sustainability impact.

The three-year fellowship provides a $65,000 annual salary, full Cornell employee benefits, and $12,000 per year for research and travel expenses. Fellows also benefit from academic mentorship, external organizational collaboration, and professional development through the Sustainability Leadership Program.

The fellowship’s emphasis on science communication, strategic career planning, collaborative leadership, and real-world impact makes it particularly valuable for researchers who want to develop beyond traditional academic research and contribute to meaningful sustainability solutions.

Interested applicants should begin identifying their proposed Cornell faculty mentor and external partner, preparing their research proposal, and contacting their four recommenders as early as possible.

The application deadline is October 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET, and all required recommendation letters must also be received by that deadline.

Applicants should carefully review every requirement before submitting because late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed, and submitted applications cannot be edited.

item.content:encoded:
Are you looking for a fully funded PhD opportunity in the United Kingdom where you can conduct research in education, childhood, youth, language and literacy, social justice, inclusion, or innovative educational methodologies?

The Sheffield Institute of Education at Sheffield Hallam University is inviting applications for White Rose-funded PhD scholarships starting in October 2027. The opportunity is particularly suitable for prospective doctoral researchers who have an original research idea aligned with the White Rose Education, Childhood, and Youth pathway.

The scholarships offer an opportunity to undertake doctoral research within a highly active research environment while benefiting from doctoral training, academic supervision, research networking, conferences, and the wider training opportunities provided through the White Rose Doctoral Training Partnership (WRDTP).

Importantly, applicants are expected to develop their own research project ideas, rather than simply selecting from a fixed list of advertised PhD projects.

According to the White Rose DTP, its studentships support social sciences doctoral research across seven partner universities and are accredited through the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC).

Opportunity Category: Scholarship / Fully Funded PhD Studentship

Deadline: 12:00 pm GMT on 13 November 2026

About the White Rose Funded PhD Scholarships

The White Rose-funded PhD scholarships provide an opportunity for prospective doctoral researchers to pursue advanced research within the social sciences.

At Sheffield Hallam University, the opportunity is hosted by the Sheffield Institute of Education (SIOE), a research environment focused on education, teaching, learning, childhood, youth, language, literacy, social justice, inclusion, and methodological innovation.

Applicants are encouraged to develop a research proposal that fits within the Education, Childhood, and Youth pathway and connects meaningfully with the research expertise available within the Sheffield Institute of Education.

The WRDTP operates as a partnership between Sheffield Hallam University and six other universities: the universities of Bradford, Hull, Leeds, Sheffield, and York, together with Manchester Metropolitan University.

For prospective applicants, this means the scholarship is not simply about obtaining financial support for a PhD. It is also an opportunity to become part of a wider doctoral training and research network.

PhD Study Starting in October 2027

The Sheffield Institute of Education is seeking applications for doctoral study beginning in October 2027.

Both full-time and part-time PhD studies are available under the scholarship opportunity.

Applicants should therefore consider which study mode is most appropriate for their circumstances, professional commitments, and research plans.

The university recommends that applicants begin preparing well before the final deadline because the application process includes contacting potential supervisors and developing a research proposal.

This is particularly important because prospective applicants are expected to identify a suitable research direction and work with the university to establish appropriate supervisory arrangements.

What Does the Scholarship Support?

The White Rose DTP studentship structure provides substantial doctoral funding.

The WRDTP states that its studentships cover UK tuition fees and maintenance at the standard UKRI rate. The partner universities have also agreed to cover the difference between UK and international tuition fees for overseas students who hold eligible studentships, meaning successful international students are not expected to personally fund the Home/International fee gap.

Depending on the applicable award route, the funding can be structured in different ways.

1. +3.5 Programme

This route provides funding for a 3.5-year PhD.

It is generally suited to applicants who already have a social sciences master’s degree and have completed substantial master’s-level research training. The WRDTP identifies applicants with a social science master’s degree and approximately 60 or more credits, or equivalent, of master’s-level social science research training as those most likely to benefit from this route.

2. +3.75 Programme

This route combines an integrated postgraduate certificate with the doctoral programme.

It is generally intended for applicants who have a social sciences master’s degree but have not completed the core research training normally expected for direct doctoral study.

3. 1+3.5 Programme

This route provides funding for a one-year master’s programme followed by a 3.5-year PhD.

It can be appropriate for applicants who do not already hold a master’s degree in the social sciences.

The appropriate route is determined according to the applicant’s previous academic and research experience and through discussions with the proposed supervisor and university.

Potential Research Areas at Sheffield Institute of Education

One of the most attractive features of this opportunity is the breadth of research topics available.

The Sheffield Institute of Education groups its research into five major clusters.

Applicants should use these areas to develop a research proposal that is academically strong, original, and clearly connected to existing research expertise.

1. Improving the Effectiveness of Educational Professionals and Enhancing Curriculum and Pedagogy

This research cluster focuses on educational professionals and the ways teaching, learning and professional practice can be improved.

Potential research topics include:

  • Teacher recruitment and retention
  • Teacher working conditions
  • Teacher wellbeing
  • Professional identities
  • Professional development
  • Professional learning
  • Mentoring
  • Evidence-informed educational practice
  • Curriculum innovation
  • Pedagogical innovation
  • Evaluation of educational interventions
  • Experiences of teachers and lecturers
  • Further education
  • Higher education
  • Educational practitioner development

A strong proposal in this area could, for example, investigate how professional development affects teacher retention, how new pedagogical approaches influence student learning, or how educational institutions can improve staff well-being.

2. Enhancing Language and Literacy Education

The second cluster examines language and literacy in their many forms and contexts.

The research area recognises that communication and literacy have become increasingly complex as education and society have become more digitally connected and culturally diverse.

Potential areas include:

  • Language learning
  • Literacy education
  • Learners’ language experiences
  • Learners’ literacy experiences
  • Digital literacy
  • Digital language practices
  • Multimodal literacies
  • Early-years literacy
  • Workplace literacy
  • English for Academic Purposes
  • English for Research and Publication Purposes
  • TESOL
  • Multilingualism
  • Global literacies

This area could be particularly relevant to researchers interested in how technology is changing literacy practices, how multilingual learners experience education, or how language affects participation and achievement.

3. Improving Childhood and Young People’s Educational and Social Experiences

The third research cluster focuses broadly on children and young people and their experiences within educational and social environments.

The research spans the educational journey from the early years through higher education.

Potential research themes include:

  • Early-years education
  • Childhood
  • Youth
  • Children’s wellbeing
  • Young people’s well-being
  • Participation in education
  • Friendships
  • Play
  • Literacy
  • STEM education
  • Outdoor education
  • Mentoring
  • Educational disadvantage
  • Young people at risk of criminal activity
  • Subject-specific educational research
  • Educational policy
  • Educational practice and provision

This cluster provides significant scope for applicants interested in the relationship between education and young people’s social, emotional, and educational experiences.

4. Promoting Social Justice and Inclusion

The fourth research cluster focuses on some of the most important contemporary questions concerning equality, inclusion, and educational disadvantage.

Research in this area examines how education can contribute to more socially just societies while addressing discrimination, exclusion, and structural disadvantage.

Potential topics include:

  • Social justice in education
  • Educational inclusion
  • Discrimination
  • Racism and educational outcomes
  • Participation and student experience
  • International student experiences
  • Internationalisation
  • Socioeconomic disadvantage
  • Educational inequality
  • Vocational skills
  • Apprenticeships
  • Disability and education
  • Youth and society
  • Social justice in higher education
  • Anti-discriminatory educational practices

Applicants interested in the relationship between education and inequality may find this cluster particularly relevant.

Research could examine, for example, how socioeconomic circumstances affect educational outcomes, how institutions can improve inclusion, or how educational policies influence disadvantaged communities.

5. Innovating in Theory and Methodology

The fifth research cluster focuses on developing new ways of thinking about and conducting education research.

This is particularly relevant to applicants who want to develop innovative methodological approaches or apply emerging technologies and research techniques to educational questions.

Potential areas include:

  • Educational theory
  • Research methodology
  • Digital technologies
  • Materialities
  • Evaluation theory
  • Evaluation methods
  • Education policy
  • Anti-oppressive methodologies
  • Creative research practices
  • Randomised controlled trials
  • Quasi-experimental methods
  • Mixed-methods research

The cluster could be particularly attractive to applicants who want to combine qualitative and quantitative approaches or develop innovative ways of studying complex educational problems.

Why Study at the Sheffield Institute of Education?

Successful applicants will become part of the Sheffield Institute of Education’s active community of researchers and doctoral students.

The institute provides an environment designed to support doctoral researchers throughout their PhD journey.

Researchers have opportunities to:

  • Interact with other postgraduate researchers
  • Collaborate on research
  • Participate in academic events
  • Attend research training
  • Develop research skills
  • Present research
  • Engage with established scholars
  • Build academic networks
  • Participate in conferences
  • Receive doctoral development support

The institute also organises training sessions covering areas such as

  • Thesis writing
  • Research methods
  • Conference participation
  • Research communication
  • Doctoral research development

These activities complement the wider training offered by the Sheffield Hallam University Doctoral School.

Doctoral Research Conference and Research Seminars

Another advantage of joining the Sheffield Institute of Education is the opportunity to engage with a broader research community.

Doctoral researchers organise an annual SIoE doctoral research conference, where postgraduate researchers can present their work in progress.

This provides an important opportunity for PhD students to

  1. Practise communicating their research.
  2. Receive feedback on developing ideas.
  3. Build confidence in academic presentations.
  4. Meet fellow doctoral researchers.
  5. Develop professional academic networks.
  6. Explore opportunities for collaboration.

The institute also hosts a research seminar series, providing opportunities for researchers to exchange ideas with scholars within Sheffield Hallam and beyond.

White Rose-funded students additionally benefit from the wider training and networking opportunities offered through the WRDTP.

Research Quality at Sheffield Hallam University

Sheffield Hallam University describes its research approach through the principle of “knowledge applied,” emphasising research with practical and real-world outcomes.

The university’s educational research has received recognition through the Research Excellence Framework (REF) 2021.

According to Sheffield Hallam’s information supplied for this opportunity:

  • The university ranked 11th for research power among 83 universities.
  • Its research environment was recognised as the best among modern universities.
  • 70% of research outputs were assessed as world-leading or internationally excellent.
  • Almost 90% of research impact was assessed as world-leading or internationally excellent.

These indicators demonstrate the research environment available to doctoral researchers and highlight the university’s emphasis on research that can generate practical impact.

Who Can Apply for the White Rose PhD Scholarship?

This opportunity is designed primarily for prospective doctoral researchers interested in social sciences research, particularly research connected with the Education, Childhood, and Youth pathway.

Applicants must satisfy both:

  • Sheffield Hallam University’s PhD entry requirements; and
  • the relevant WRDTP/ESRC eligibility requirements.

The WRDTP states that applicants must hold an offer for a PhD place in an eligible school or department and must undertake a social sciences research project falling within the ESRC’s remit.

Applicants are also expected to meet the required academic threshold.

The ESRC minimum requirement is generally equivalent to a good honours degree at a first-class or upper-second-class level, although equivalent international qualifications can be considered. Applicants must also satisfy their university’s individual entry requirements.

Can International Students Apply?

Yes. International applicants can be eligible for WRDTP studentships, subject to the applicable eligibility rules and the competitive allocation of awards.

The WRDTP states that international applicants are eligible, but the ESRC limits the proportion of WRDTP awards available to international candidates to 30% of awards in a year. Consequently, universities place limits on the number of international applications they can nominate.

This makes the opportunity highly competitive for applicants from outside the United Kingdom.

International applicants should therefore pay particular attention to the following:

  • Academic eligibility
  • Research proposal quality
  • Alignment with the research pathway
  • Supervisor fit
  • Sheffield Hallam’s admission requirements
  • WRDTP eligibility
  • International student procedures
  • Immigration requirements

The WRDTP also confirms that its partner universities cover the difference between UK and international tuition fees for overseas studentship holders. However, visa costs, the Immigration Health Surcharge, flights, and other relocation expenses are not covered by the UKRI studentship.

What Kind of Academic Background Is Suitable?

Applicants should have an academic background that enables them to undertake doctoral research in the social sciences and meet the entry requirements of the relevant Sheffield Hallam programme.

Depending on the proposed research topic, suitable academic backgrounds could include fields such as the following:

  • Education
  • Childhood studies
  • Youth studies
  • Sociology
  • Social policy
  • Psychology
  • Language and literacy
  • Linguistics
  • TESOL
  • International education
  • Educational leadership
  • Development studies
  • Social sciences
  • Related disciplines

However, applicants should not assume that a particular degree automatically guarantees eligibility.

The strongest approach is to demonstrate a clear connection between your academic background, research experience, proposed project, and the Sheffield Institute of Education’s research expertise.

How to Develop a Strong PhD Research Proposal

Because applicants are encouraged to submit their own project ideas, the research proposal is likely to be one of the most important elements of the application.

A strong proposal should demonstrate that you understand the problem you want to investigate and can explain why the research matters.

Consider including the following:

1. Research title

Create a clear and specific title that communicates the central issue being investigated.

2. Background and context

Explain the problem and provide sufficient context for the proposed research.

3. Research problem

Identify the specific gap, challenge, or unresolved issue that your research intends to address.

4. Research questions

Develop focused research questions that can realistically be answered through a PhD.

5. Literature review

Demonstrate familiarity with existing scholarship and explain how your research will contribute to it.

6. Research methodology

Explain how you intend to collect and analyse evidence.

Depending on the research question, this could involve the following:

  • Qualitative research
  • Quantitative research
  • Mixed methods
  • Interviews
  • Surveys
  • Case studies
  • Document analysis
  • Ethnographic approaches
  • Experimental approaches
  • Quasi-experimental approaches
  • Participatory research
  • Creative research methods

7. Original contribution

Explain what will be new about your research.

A doctoral project needs to make a meaningful contribution to knowledge, theory, methodology, policy, or practice.

8. Real-world impact

Explain how your findings could contribute to education, policy, professional practice, communities, or broader society.

9. Fit with Sheffield Hallam

Clearly demonstrate why the Sheffield Institute of Education is an appropriate environment for the project.

This should include consideration of relevant research clusters and potential supervisors.

How to Apply for the White Rose PhD Scholarship

Applicants do not submit their scholarship application directly to the White Rose Doctoral Training Partnership.

Instead, applications for the WRDTP awards are submitted through Sheffield Hallam University.

The application process consists of two important stages.

Stage 1: Pre-Application

Prospective applicants should contact Dr. Lisa McGrath at Sheffield Hallam University if they are interested in applying.

The university advises applicants to provide a working proposal using the WRDTP Studentship Application Form, including the research proposal in Section 2, “About Your Project.”

Dr. Lisa McGrath can assist prospective applicants in identifying a suitable supervisor.

This stage is important because applicants need sufficient time to:

  • Develop their research proposal.
  • Identify potential supervisory expertise.
  • Discuss the proposed research.
  • Refine the project.
  • Complete the relevant studentship materials.
  • Prepare the formal PhD application.

Applicants should not leave this process until the final days before the deadline.

The university specifically warns that, because of high demand, colleagues may not be able to respond to enquiries received close to the submission deadline.

Stage 2: Formal PhD Application

After the pre-application stage, candidates must submit a formal application for a PhD at Sheffield Hallam University.

The scholarship application and the university’s PhD admission process are therefore connected but should not be treated as exactly the same application.

The WRDTP also confirms that the studentship application form is separate from the university’s application for a PhD place.

Applicants should carefully complete both processes and ensure that all required documents are submitted.

Important Application Deadline

The closing date stated for the Sheffield Hallam application is:

12:00 pm GMT on 13 November 2026

No late applications will be accepted.

Applicants should therefore aim to submit their application before the final deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

This is especially important for international applicants, prospective doctoral researchers who need supervisor discussions, and candidates whose proposals require substantial revision.

Key Information at a Glance

Detail Information
Opportunity White Rose Funded PhD Scholarships
University Sheffield Hallam University
Host Sheffield Institute of Education
PhD start October 2027
Study mode Full-time and part-time
Main research area Education, Childhood, and Youth
Funding partnership White Rose Doctoral Training Partnership
Funding body ESRC-supported WRDTP
Research field Social sciences
International applicants Eligible, subject to WRDTP rules
Application route Sheffield Hallam University
Deadline 12:00 pm GMT, 13 November 2026
Late applications Not accepted

Important Advice for Prospective Applicants

If you are seriously considering applying, start preparing early.

A competitive doctoral funding application requires more than simply meeting the minimum academic requirements.

Focus on research fit

Your proposal should clearly connect with one or more of the Sheffield Institute of Education’s research clusters.

Identify a suitable supervisor

Supervisor alignment can be particularly important for a self-designed doctoral project.

Research the academic expertise available at Sheffield Hallam and explain why your chosen research environment is appropriate.

Make your proposal specific

Avoid proposals that attempt to investigate an excessively broad issue.

Instead, identify a manageable research problem that can realistically be investigated during a PhD.

Demonstrate originality

Explain what existing research has not adequately addressed and how your project will contribute something new.

Think about impact

Consider how your research could benefit:

  • Educational institutions
  • Teachers
  • Students
  • Children and young people
  • Policymakers
  • Communities
  • Researchers
  • Practitioners

Check international eligibility carefully

International applicants should review the WRDTP’s specific requirements because international students are subject to the annual 30% allocation limit.

APPLY HERE

Additional Opportunities Through the White Rose DTP

The value of a WRDTP studentship extends beyond tuition funding and a maintenance stipend.

The partnership provides doctoral researchers with training and development opportunities designed to strengthen research and methodological and professional skills.

The WRDTP describes its broader mission as equipping doctoral researchers with high levels of methodological and data literacy and preparing them for research leadership.

Depending on eligibility and the terms of the award, funded researchers can also access additional opportunities relating to activities such as the following:

  • Research training
  • Conference participation
  • Overseas fieldwork
  • Overseas institutional visits
  • Professional placements
  • Research networking
  • Skills development

For example, WRDTP information confirms that additional funding can support eligible overseas fieldwork and institutional visits, subject to specific requirements and available funding.

The partnership also incorporates placement opportunities into its doctoral training structure for applicable cohorts, providing researchers with opportunities to develop professional skills beyond traditional academic research.

Why This Opportunity Could Be Valuable for International Researchers

For researchers outside the United Kingdom, this PhD scholarship could offer several important advantages.

First, it provides an opportunity to pursue doctoral research within a UK university and become part of an established international research community.

Second, eligible international students can benefit from the WRDTP arrangement under which the partner universities cover the difference between UK and international tuition fees for overseas studentship holders.

Third, researchers can access the wider training, networking, and professional development opportunities available through the White Rose DTP.

However, applicants should budget separately for costs that are not covered by the studentship, including visa-related expenses, the Immigration Health Surcharge, flights, and relocation costs.

Who Is Most Likely to Be a Strong Candidate?

The opportunity could be particularly suitable for:

  • Graduates interested in pursuing a career in academic research.
  • Education researchers with a clearly defined research question.
  • Teachers and education professionals interested in doctoral study.
  • Researchers interested in childhood and youth.
  • Language and literacy researchers.
  • Social justice and inclusion researchers.
  • Researchers examining educational inequality.
  • Applicants interested in educational policy and practice.
  • Researchers interested in digital education and technology.
  • Candidates interested in innovative research methodology.
  • International researchers seeking a UK-based PhD.
  • Applicants with a strong academic record and research potential.

The strongest candidates will be those who can combine academic preparation with a compelling, original, and feasible research project that fits the expertise and research priorities of the Sheffield Institute of Education.

Visit HERE for more information about the White Rose-Funded PhD Scholarships 2027 at Sheffield Hallam University.

Conclusion

The White Rose-Funded PhD scholarships at Sheffield Hallam University’s Sheffield Institute of Education represent a significant opportunity for aspiring doctoral researchers who want to conduct high-quality research in education, childhood, youth, language, literacy, social justice, inclusion, or research methodology.

The opportunity stands out because applicants are encouraged to develop their own research ideas, allowing candidates to shape a doctoral project around a research problem that genuinely interests them while aligning it with the Education, Childhood, and Youth pathway and the expertise available at Sheffield Hallam.

The funding can provide substantial support through tuition fees and a maintenance stipend, while eligible international students can benefit from arrangements covering the difference between UK and international tuition fees. The wider White Rose DTP also provides doctoral training, research development, networking, and professional opportunities.

Prospective applicants should not wait until the deadline to begin. The process requires a research proposal, supervisor engagement, and a formal PhD application, making early preparation particularly important.

The application deadline is 12:00 pm GMT on 13 November 2026, and late applications will not be accepted.

For official information, applicants should consult the Sheffield Hallam University PhD scholarships information and the White Rose Doctoral Training Partnership studentship information before submitting an application.

item.content:encoded:
The Water Research Foundation (WRF) has announced a new Research Priority Program opportunity seeking research proposals that will examine the return on investment (ROI) of internships, apprenticeships, and workforce development programs. The initiative is designed to help utilities better understand whether these programs deliver measurable organizational value and how they can contribute to workforce retention, recruitment, career advancement, and reduced dependence on external labor.

With $250,000 in funding available, the research opportunity is particularly relevant to researchers, academic institutions, water and wastewater utilities, workforce development specialists, and organizations with expertise in human resources, talent development, organizational performance, and utility workforce management.

The research will focus on developing evidence-based approaches that utilities can use to assess the effectiveness and financial value of investments in internships, apprenticeships, and other employee development initiatives.

The application deadline is September 14, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. Mountain Time (US & Canada).

Opportunity Overview

The Water Research Foundation’s Research Priority Program is inviting proposals under Research Priority Program project 5414, titled “Return on Investment for Internships, Apprenticeships, and Development Programs.”

The project recognizes that water and wastewater utilities face significant workforce challenges, including the need to recruit skilled employees, retain workers in critical positions, fill vacancies efficiently, develop internal talent, and reduce dependence on external recruitment.

Internships, apprenticeships, and professional development programs can play an important role in addressing these challenges. However, organizations often need stronger evidence to demonstrate the financial and operational value of these investments.

This research project aims to address that gap by developing a clearer understanding of the measurable return utilities receive from investing in workforce development programs.

The selected research team will therefore be expected to investigate how these programs influence important workforce and organizational outcomes while developing practical tools that utilities can use when making investment decisions.

Funding Available

A total of $250,000 is available for the research project.

The funding is intended to support research that can generate practical and credible evidence about the value of internships, apprenticeships, and development programs within the utility sector.

Applicants should carefully review the official Research Priority Program guidelines, research request for proposals, budget requirements, financial and grant management guidance, and other application documents before preparing a submission.

Research Objectives

The central purpose of the opportunity is to quantify the return on investment associated with internships, apprenticeships, and development programs.

The project has three major objectives.

1. Quantify the Return on Investment

The research should examine the financial and organizational returns associated with investments in internships, apprenticeships, and development programs.

This means moving beyond simply determining whether a program exists or how many participants it serves. Instead, the research should help utilities understand the measurable value generated by these workforce initiatives.

Potential areas of analysis may include:

  • Costs associated with establishing and operating development programs.
  • Recruitment and onboarding costs.
  • Employee retention.
  • Workforce turnover.
  • Time required to fill vacant positions.
  • Internal promotion and advancement.
  • Development of employees for critical roles.
  • Reduced dependence on external recruitment.
  • Workforce productivity and organizational performance.
  • Long-term talent pipeline development.
  • Potential savings associated with improved retention and internal mobility.

By quantifying these outcomes, the research can help utilities make stronger evidence-based decisions about whether and how much to invest in workforce development initiatives.

2. Assess Effectiveness in Critical and High-Turnover Roles

The project will also examine how internships, apprenticeships, and development programs support positions that are particularly difficult to recruit for or retain.

Utilities often depend on employees with specialized technical knowledge and experience. When these employees leave, organizations may face significant challenges in finding qualified replacements.

The research will therefore assess whether workforce development programs can contribute to better outcomes in critical and high-turnover roles.

Important areas of investigation include:

  • Employee retention: Whether employees who participate in internships, apprenticeships, or development programs remain with the organization for longer periods.
  • Time to fill: Whether developing talent internally can reduce the amount of time required to fill vacant positions.
  • Internal advancement: Whether participants are more likely to progress into higher-level or more specialized positions within the organization.
  • Reduced reliance on external labor: Whether organizations can build stronger internal talent pipelines and reduce their dependence on external recruitment.

These findings could provide utilities with practical evidence about which workforce development strategies are most effective for addressing persistent staffing challenges.

3. Develop a Business Case Framework and Decision-Support Tools

Another important objective is to develop a framework that utilities can use to evaluate, communicate, and justify investments in internships, apprenticeships, and development programs.

This is particularly important because workforce development initiatives can sometimes be difficult to justify using traditional short-term financial measurements.

A comprehensive business case framework could help decision-makers assess both the costs and benefits of these programs.

The research is also expected to contribute to decision-support tools that utilities can use when evaluating workforce development investments.

Such tools could potentially help organizations:

  1. Estimate program costs.
  2. Identify relevant workforce outcomes.
  3. Measure retention and turnover.
  4. Calculate recruitment-related savings.
  5. Assess internal advancement.
  6. Compare different workforce development approaches.
  7. Communicate results to senior management.
  8. Support future workforce investment decisions.

The ultimate goal is to provide utilities with practical resources rather than research findings that remain purely academic.

Why This Research Matters

The water sector depends heavily on a capable and sustainable workforce. As utilities compete for skilled professionals and technical workers, organizations need effective strategies for attracting, developing, and retaining talent.

Internships and apprenticeships can provide pathways for individuals to enter the water and wastewater workforce, while professional development programs can help existing employees acquire new skills and prepare for advancement.

However, organizations may face questions such as:

  • How much does an internship program actually return to the organization?
  • Do apprentices remain with the utility after completing their training?
  • Are employees who participate in development programs more likely to advance internally?
  • Can workforce development reduce employee turnover?
  • Can developing employees internally reduce recruitment costs?
  • How quickly can an organization recover its investment in a development program?
  • Which workforce development approaches generate the strongest results?
  • How can utility leaders demonstrate the value of these programs to senior management and other stakeholders?

The proposed research is intended to help answer these questions through systematic analysis.

Key Areas the Research Could Examine

The opportunity has several interconnected areas that applicants should consider when developing their research proposals.

Workforce Retention

Employee retention is a major component of workforce sustainability.

The research will examine whether participation in internships, apprenticeships, and development programs contributes to employees remaining with an organization for longer periods.

A better understanding of retention outcomes could help utilities determine whether workforce development investments can reduce turnover-related costs.

Recruitment and Time to Fill

Vacancies in specialized utility positions can remain open for extended periods when organizations struggle to identify qualified candidates.

The project will assess whether workforce development programs can help shorten the time required to fill critical positions.

Developing employees internally could potentially create a more predictable talent pipeline and reduce recruitment delays.

Internal Career Advancement

Career progression is another important area of investigation.

Development programs may help employees acquire the technical, managerial, and professional competencies required to move into more advanced roles.

The research will therefore consider the extent to which these programs contribute to internal advancement and career mobility.

Reduced Dependence on External Labor

Organizations frequently turn to external recruitment when qualified workers cannot be found internally.

By building structured talent pipelines through internships, apprenticeships, and employee development programs, utilities may be able to fill more positions from within their existing workforce.

The research will examine whether this approach can reduce reliance on external labor and associated recruitment expenses.

Expected Practical Value for Utilities

One of the strongest features of the opportunity is its focus on producing results that can be applied directly within the utility sector.

The research should help organizations make more informed decisions about workforce investments.

Potential benefits include:

  • Better understanding of the financial value of workforce development.
  • Improved workforce planning.
  • Stronger succession planning.
  • More effective recruitment strategies.
  • Improved employee retention.
  • Greater internal mobility.
  • More efficient filling of critical positions.
  • Reduced recruitment and turnover costs.
  • Stronger evidence for workforce development budgets.
  • Improved communication between workforce managers and senior leadership.
  • Better tools for comparing different development programs.

Potential Participants in the Research

The Water Research Foundation indicates that several utilities and organizations have already expressed interest in participating in the research.

The listed potential participants include:

  • Ann Arbor Water in Michigan.
  • City of Decatur, Illinois.
  • King County Wastewater Treatment Division in Washington.
  • Orange County Utilities in Florida.
  • Resource Renew (WLSSD) in Minnesota.

The Foundation notes that this information is updated frequently as additional utilities are encouraged to volunteer throughout the RFP cycle.

The involvement of utilities can be valuable because the research requires practical insight into workforce development programs and their organizational outcomes.

Application Deadline

Applicants must submit their proposals by:

September 14, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. Mountain Time (US & Canada).

Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin preparing their submissions, particularly because the application requires several supporting documents and financial information.

Application Documents and Resources

Applicants are expected to consult the official materials provided by the Water Research Foundation before preparing their proposals.

The available documents include:

2026 Guidelines for Research Priority Program

These guidelines provide important information about the Research Priority Program and the requirements applicants need to follow when developing proposals.

Certification and Assurance Form

Applicants should review and complete the relevant certification and assurance documentation required for the proposal.

Co-Funding Support Form

Where applicable, applicants should use the co-funding documentation to provide information concerning additional financial support.

Current and Pending Form

This form is intended to capture information about current and pending research or funding commitments relevant to the application.

Financial and Grant Management Researcher Guidelines

Applicants should review these guidelines to understand the financial and grant management expectations associated with WRF-funded research.

Financial Grant Management Capabilities Form

This document addresses the applicant’s financial and grant management capabilities.

Instructions for Budget Preparation

Applicants should follow the specified requirements when developing the research budget.

Proposal Budget Form

A proposal budget spreadsheet is provided as part of the application materials.

RFP-5414

The official RFP-5414 document contains the specific request for proposals for the research project concerning the return on investment of internships, apprenticeships, and development programs.

How to Prepare a Strong Proposal

Applicants interested in this opportunity should ensure that their proposals directly respond to the research objectives.

A strong proposal should clearly explain:

  1. The research problem — Identify the workforce development challenge being addressed.
  2. The research methodology — Explain how the research will collect and analyze relevant information.
  3. The ROI approach — Demonstrate how the research will quantify financial and organizational returns.
  4. The workforce outcomes — Explain how retention, time to fill, internal advancement, and external labor dependence will be assessed.
  5. Utility relevance — Show how the findings can be applied by water and wastewater utilities.
  6. Practical deliverables — Clearly identify the framework, tools, models, or other outputs that will be produced.
  7. Budget justification — Demonstrate how the proposed funding will support the research activities.
  8. Potential utility participation — Where relevant, explain how participating utilities can contribute data, expertise, or testing environments.

The proposal should demonstrate not only academic rigor but also practical usefulness for utilities making real-world workforce decisions.

APPLY HERE

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity is particularly relevant to organizations and research teams working at the intersection of:

  • Water and wastewater utilities.
  • Workforce development.
  • Human resources.
  • Apprenticeships and internships.
  • Organizational development.
  • Talent management.
  • Employee retention.
  • Workforce planning.
  • Utility management.
  • Labor economics.
  • Organizational research.
  • Public-sector workforce development.
  • Higher education and applied research.
  • Training and professional development.
  • Recruitment and talent pipelines.

Applicants should carefully consult the official RFP and 2026 Research Priority Program guidelines for the definitive eligibility requirements, institutional requirements, proposal conditions, and other participation criteria.

Visit HERE for more information about the Water Research Foundation Grant.

Geographic Eligibility

The information provided for the opportunity does not state a general restriction limiting applicants by race, ethnicity, or nationality.

The potential participating utilities currently listed on the opportunity page are based in the United States, including organizations in Michigan, Illinois, Washington, and Florida.

However, applicants should rely on the official RFP and program guidelines to determine whether their particular institution, organization, research team, or proposed partnership meets the eligibility and participation requirements.

Important Contact

The Water Research Foundation identifies Alice Jariz, PE as the WRF RFP contact for this research opportunity.

Applicants who need clarification about the research request should consult the official RFP and the Foundation’s designated contact information before submitting their proposals.

Conclusion

The Water Research Foundation’s $250,000 Research Priority Program opportunity on the Return on Investment for Internships, Apprenticeships, and Development Programs presents an important opportunity to generate practical evidence about how workforce development investments can strengthen the water and wastewater sector.

By examining retention, time to fill, internal advancement, and dependence on external labor, the research seeks to move beyond general claims about the value of internships, apprenticeships, and employee development. Instead, it aims to establish measurable evidence that utilities can use when making workforce and financial decisions.

The development of a business case framework and decision-support tools could be particularly valuable, giving utilities practical mechanisms for evaluating workforce development programs and communicating their value to organizational leadership.

With $250,000 available and a deadline of September 14, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. Mountain Time, eligible and interested research organizations should review the full RFP, program guidelines, budget requirements, and supporting forms carefully and begin preparing their proposals well before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Cancer Health Drivers Training Program at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill offers postdoctoral training on cross-cutting health disparity issues across the cancer continuum, from etiology and primary prevention to survivorship. The program includes the major cancers and addresses risk factors, epidemiological bases of disparities, detection, epidemiology, research methods, prevention and control, promotion, screening, communication, community-based participatory research and policy.

Fellows receive up to two years of funding. At the end of each year, each fellow’s performance is evaluated and funding for the next year depends on the progress made. Fellows are assigned faculty mentors in more than one discipline and benefit from the UNC’s highly collaborative, productive and multidisciplinary faculty.
